paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus is stronger than anything that holds people down, and the Pharisees had Him all backwards. A man who couldn't see or speak was set free, and the crowds asked, "Could this be the Son of David?" The Pharisees said it was Beelzebul, the prince of demons. Jesus showed that made no sense, because a kingdom "divided against itself" cannot stand (Matthew 12:22-26).

Jesus says, "But if I drive out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you." (Matthew 12:28) Then He says, "He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters." (Matthew 12:30) Friend, there's no standing off to the side with Jesus. He also warns that "the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven." (Matthew 12:31) I think that's a serious one, so I'm not going to joke about it.

Then Jesus brings it home to the baker's own mouth. "A tree is known by its fruit," and "out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks." (Matthew 12:33-34) Our words show what's packed inside us, and "men will give an account on the day of judgment for every careless word they have spoken." (Matthew 12:36) So, friend, fill up on the Word, because what goes in is what comes out, and the One who set that man free is the One worth following.
